projects.name: Orbit Shelf
projects.purpose: Collect and search personal notes with source links and writing-language metadata.
projects.relationship: New application inspired by documented navigation and source-preservation goals; not a recovered Orbit implementation.

projects.name: Word Weave
projects.purpose: Rearrange writing while keeping the original and exporting a separate remix.
projects.inspiredBy: Language work and Tiny Babel / TBCL
projects.relationship: New writing application inspired by source/transform separation; not a TBCL interpreter or a model of linguistic truth.

projects.name: Pattern Garden
projects.purpose: Create geometric patterns with keyboard controls, rotation, mirroring, undo, SVG, and text export.
projects.inspiredBy: Geometry, codecs, and creative world-building ideas
projects.relationship: New creative geometry application; not a representation of a particular culture or a physical-theory result.

projects.name: Small Steps
projects.purpose: Plan one next step and retain dated snapshots of actions, outcomes, assumptions, and unknowns.
projects.inspiredBy: The user’s I/R/P/O working method and bounded experiment records
projects.relationship: New self-directed planning application; not a model that scores people or predicts well-being.

projects.name: Source Compare
projects.purpose: Compare exact text lines while retaining both original and revised text and optional source metadata.
projects.relationship: New exact text-comparison utility; line matches do not establish semantic equivalence, translation quality, or research truth.

projects.name: Computational Chorus
projects.purpose: Project research equations and computational-linguistics ideas into exact, speakable, mnemonic, and procedural musical forms.
projects.inspiredBy: Language Quality, I/R/P/O, Tiny Babel/TBCL, Cross-Carrier Wave, P vs NP research boundaries, human-context modeling, Unicode/Float64 transport, Musilanguage, and bounded claim practice
projects.relationship: Mnemonic and creative synthesis tool. Alliteration, sonification, and compression are memory aids; they do not create proof or transfer evidence between domains.
